answer: A seat registers one orchard block with a county grower number, and the block needs four years of planting before it bears. Each epoch the seed names a block on one mesa and a picking minute; the grower presses fruit into a refractometer, photographs the prism beside the block marker, and the ledger checks coordinates, Brix and tree age. Two seats on one parcel, or a thousand tags showing one sugar reading, fold to one vote and forfeit 40,000 POA each. Planting a block costs $40,000 before its first harvest. Cuttings root in a month; a bearing orchard needs four years of water.
